mutants.title: the launcher spells the control flag itself, so a typo in run.sh silently produces a pi that is not a citizen and reports nothing
mutants.subject: run.sh

mutants.title: without the shift the dispatcher verb stays in the forwarded argv and `pi` arrives at the vendor as a prompt argument
mutants.subject: run.sh

mutants.title: injecting the flag AFTER the operator argv puts it behind a positional prompt, where pi reads it as data instead of standing up a control socket
mutants.subject: run.sh

mutants.title: a launcher that also injects operator taste stops being a spelling and starts deciding the session (Rule 9)
mutants.subject: run.sh

mutants.title: an unquoted forward word-splits the operator argv and drops empty elements, so a quoted prompt silently becomes several arguments
mutants.subject: run.sh

mutants.title: forking instead of exec leaves run.sh as a parent that supervises nothing and owns neither the terminal nor the exit
mutants.subject: run.sh

mutants.title: an absent vendor that exits 0 is the false success this repo refuses: nothing launched and the caller was told it worked
mutants.subject: run.sh
find:
echo "         'entwurf pi' launches the pi coding agent; it does not install one." >&2
      exit 1
replace:
echo "         'entwurf pi' launches the pi coding agent; it does not install one." >&2
      exit 0

mutants.title: a sentinel that is set but not exported is invisible to the re-entered child, so the recursion fence never fires and the terminal hangs
mutants.subject: run.sh

mutants.title: with the fence removed a PATH `pi` that shells back here spins forever, and the symptom is a hung terminal rather than an error
mutants.subject: run.sh
find:
if [ -n "${ENTWURF_PI_LAUNCH_ACTIVE:-}" ]; then
      echo "entwurf: recursive managed launch detected (ENTWURF_PI_LAUNCH_ACTIVE is already set)." >&2
replace:
if false; then
      echo "entwurf: recursive managed launch detected (ENTWURF_PI_LAUNCH_ACTIVE is already set)." >&2
